paraphrase: Two finite, universally accessible, explanation-sound models separate the commitments: (1) every existence fact at every world has some stipulated explanation and some individual exists at world false and at every world, yet not every existent has a distinct existing cause (at least one existent at some world lacks one); and (2) every contingent existent's existence fact has some stipulated explanation, an individual that exists at world false but not at some world (so the contingent-only principle applies non-vacuously there) and a necessarily existing individual both exist, yet some existent at some world lacks any explanation of its existence fact. Thus an existence-PSR need not entail that every existent is externally caused, and a contingent-only existence-PSR need not entail the existence-PSR. The certified type does not say that no existent is caused, that any explanation is intrinsic, or which existent in (2) is unexplained; the concrete witnesses have those further properties, but they are not part of this statement. Reasons and their adequacy are stipulated, not vindicated.
